# Handle an uncertain result

Source: <https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/handling-uncertain>

An order is `uncertain` when we sent it and its receipt at the exchange is unconfirmed: the connection dropped, the exchange did not reply in time, or the broker refused it with a reason it doesn't publish. The order may or may not be at the exchange, so it is recorded as `uncertain`, not as failed. Treating it as failed and placing it again could buy the shares twice.

## What you see

`POST /v1/orders` returns `201 Created` with `state` set to `uncertain`, and you receive an `order.uncertain` [event](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/webhooks). The `reason` field describes the state.

We never resubmit an uncertain order. It stays on your list with its `id`, and it counts in full against your [daily order value](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/limits).

## What to do

1. Don't place the same order again under a new `Idempotency-Key`.
2. Wait for its next event, or retrieve it with `GET /v1/orders/{id}`.
3. Act on the state it moves to:

| New state | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `pending`, `partially_filled`, `filled` | The exchange has the order. | Nothing. It continues like any other order. |
| `rejected` | The broker or the exchange didn't accept it. | Read `reject_reason`. |
| `refused` | It never reached the exchange. | If you still want the order, place it again with a new `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `cancelled` | The exchange had it and cancelled it. | Nothing. |

Retrying with the same key is safe while you wait. It returns `200 OK` with the order as it is now.

You can't cancel an uncertain order. A cancel returns `409 order_not_cancelable` until the order's state is known.

## How it resolves

About every 30 seconds we check with the broker each uncertain order that hasn't changed for [the longest `POST /v1/orders` takes to answer](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/limits#how-long-a-request-can-take). When the broker holds exactly one open order that matches yours and was received while we were sending it, we record it as yours and move it to `pending` or `partially_filled`. Our operations team reconciles every order this check cannot match directly with the broker, and records it as held, rejected or never received. If the broker refused an uncertain order, or tells us it expired, we record it as `rejected`, with `reject_reason` `rejected_by_exchange`: no shares traded, and the order is final. If you still want it, place it again with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

A `pending` order also becomes `uncertain` if the broker returns another order's report when asked about it. We record nothing from that report, the automatic check does not change the order, and our operations team reconciles it against the broker's records. A `partially_filled` order stays `partially_filled` in that case, because its fills are already recorded. We check with the broker again at the next check. If a partly filled order stops changing, [contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#report-a-problem) with its `id`.

Our operations team works from 9:00 to 17:00 West Africa Time (WAT), Monday to Friday. It reconciles an uncertain order the same business day, or the next business day if the order becomes uncertain outside those hours. To ask about one, [contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#report-a-problem) with its `id`.

## Identical orders while one is unresolved

While an order is unresolved, we refuse an identical order on the same account under a new key: the same `symbol`, `side`, `quantity`, `type`, `time_in_force` and `price_kobo`, whatever its `client_reference`. You get `409 similar_order_unresolved`, and we store nothing, so your new key stays free. We do this because the broker doesn't echo our reference back, and the broker's report does not identify which of two identical orders it holds.

An order is unresolved while it is `uncertain`, or while it still reads `sending` after its request has ended, whether or not you received an answer. A request ends at most [the longest any request stays open](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/limits#how-long-a-request-can-take) after the order's `created_at`. An order left `sending` has an outcome that was not recorded, and it resolves as an `uncertain` order does. We send a `201`, `422 order_rejected` or `503 order_not_sent` only once the outcome is recorded, so an order left `sending` never follows one of them: your request was answered `503 outcome_not_recorded`, or it ended without an answer that gives the order's outcome. Until the order resolves, an identical one is refused. To have it resolved sooner, [contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#report-a-problem) with its `id`.

An order whose request is still in progress is not counted. An identical order sent under a new key during that request is sent too, and both can trade. Use one key for each order, and reuse it on every retry.

The error's `order` holds the unresolved order's `id`. Retrieve it until it resolves:

- If it becomes `pending`, `partially_filled` or `filled`, the exchange has it. If your new request repeats it, don't send it: that would place a second order. If your new request is a separate order, send it again with the key from the request that got the `409`.
- If it becomes `rejected`, `refused` or `cancelled`, it's final. Check its `filled_quantity` first: shares that traded before it ended are already bought or sold. Then, if you still want the order, send your new request again with the key from the request that got the `409`.

## Applications and allocations

Applications and allocations can also become `uncertain`, for the same reasons. An application waiting for its account (`documents_required` or `submitted`) also becomes `uncertain` if the broker later says, twice with the same answer, that it holds no application under the reference it gave, or, giving no account, writes a sentence about it we have no meaning for. We never resubmit them, and our operations team reconciles them with the broker.

| Resource | While uncertain | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| Application | Nothing to do. Retrieve it later. Our operations team reconciles it the same business day, or the next business day if it becomes uncertain outside 9:00 to 17:00 WAT, Monday to Friday. The same holds for an application still `sending` after its request has ended. | `documents_required` or `submitted` if the broker has it, which then becomes `submitted` once its four documents arrive, then `opened`, or `rejected` if the broker declines it. `unplaced` if the broker does not hold it: it never received it, refused it with a reason it doesn't publish, or no longer holds it. [Contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) before you send it again. |
| Allocation | Its amount stays reserved in your wallet. | `booked`, or `rejected` with `reject_reason` `not_booked` and the amount returned to your wallet. |

## Identical allocations while one is unresolved

While an allocation is unresolved, we refuse another allocation to the same `account` for the same `amount_kobo` under a new key, whatever its `client_reference`. You get `409 similar_allocation_unresolved`, and we store nothing, so your new key stays free. We do this because the broker may already have booked the first.

An allocation is unresolved while it is `uncertain`, or while it still reads `sending` after its request has ended. A request ends at most [the longest any request stays open](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/limits#how-long-a-request-can-take) after the allocation's `created_at`. An allocation left `sending` has an outcome that was not recorded. We send a `201`, `403 feature_not_enabled`, `422 allocation_rejected` or `503 allocation_not_sent` only once the outcome is recorded, so an allocation left `sending` never follows one of them: your request was answered `503 outcome_not_recorded`, or it ended without an answer that gives the allocation's outcome. Our operations team reconciles it with the broker, as it does an `uncertain` one. No automatic check resolves an allocation. The team reconciles an unresolved allocation the same business day, or the next business day if it becomes unresolved outside 9:00 to 17:00 WAT, Monday to Friday.

An allocation whose request is still in progress is not counted. A second allocation sent under a new key during that request is sent too, and both can be booked. Use one key for each allocation, and reuse it on every retry.

The error's `allocation` holds the unresolved allocation's `id`. Wait for its `allocation.booked` or `allocation.rejected` event, or retrieve it until it resolves:

- If it becomes `booked`, the broker has it. If your new request repeats it, don't send it: that would fund the account twice. If your new request is a separate allocation, send it again with the key from the request that got the `409`. The allocation's `id` and `client_reference` identify it in your records.
- If it becomes `rejected`, the amount has been returned to your wallet. If you still want the allocation, send your new request again with the key from the request that got the `409`.
